buying out siblings' share of mom's house
estate.a: Most families agree in writing, before ordering a report, to rely on one independent appraisal, and settle two points in advance: the date the value is as of, and whether the selling costs the buying heir avoids are shared. If the buying heir is also the personal representative, they are selling to themselves as a fiduciary, so the price and the other heirs' agreement should be documented.
estate.pathTitle: What Happens If Heirs Disagree on Selling a House?

estate.q: What does it cost the estate if we keep arguing about the house?
alts: carrying costs inherited house delay
cost of waiting to sell estate property
why delaying the sale hurts heirs
expenses while heirs decide
estate.a: Delay has real costs. While heirs deliberate, the house still runs up mortgage payments, property taxes, insurance, maintenance and utilities, and may deteriorate, and those costs reduce the estate's value for everyone. A useful step is to document the monthly costs, lay out each option (sell now, sell later, buyout, rent), get an independent valuation and set a reasonable deadline for a decision.
estate.pathTitle: What Happens If Heirs Disagree on Selling a House?

estate.q: Should we rent out mom's house instead of selling it?
alts: rent inherited house or sell
keeping an inherited house as a rental
heirs want to rent the family home
renting estate property pros and cons
estate.a: It can work, but renting is a business decision, not passive income. It means landlord duties, maintenance, insurance and tax reporting, and co-owning a rental among several heirs often leads to disputes. Renting before selling can also complicate taxes, such as depreciation recapture. Get a realistic picture of carrying costs and management work, and talk with a CPA, before committing.
estate.pathTitle: Deciding What to Do With the Property

estate.q: What is a date-of-death appraisal and why do we need one?
alts: date of death value house
appraisal as of the date of death
why get an appraisal after a parent dies
estate appraisal purpose
How is real estate valued for probate?
what value is used for the house in probate
how do you value a house for an estate inventory
estate.a: It estimates the house's fair market value as of the day the owner died. That number sets the heirs' new tax basis for a later sale, goes into the estate inventory, feeds any estate tax return, and gives heirs an independent value to divide the estate by, for example when one heir keeps the house. It is easiest to support when done soon after the death.
estate.pathTitle: Date-of-Death Valuation & Estate Property Appraisals

estate.q: Is an appraisal legally required when someone dies in Washington?
alts: does probate require an appraisal Washington
must the executor get a certified appraisal
appraisal required for estate inventory
Do we have to pay for an appraisal on dad's house?
estate.a: No. Washington requires the personal representative to value estate property as of the date of death in the inventory, but does not require a certified appraisal. An appraisal is the value that holds up if heirs, creditors or tax authorities question it, so it is the usual choice when taxes, a dispute or a buyout are involved. The estate attorney can say whether your case needs one.
estate.pathTitle: Date-of-Death Valuation & Estate Property Appraisals

estate.q: How much does an appraisal cost for an estate house?
alts: estate appraisal cost Washington
price of a date of death appraisal
what does a probate appraisal cost
appraisal fee inherited house
estate.a: The site puts formal appraisals for estate properties typically at $400 to $800 or more, depending on the property's complexity, location and purpose. The cost is usually justified when the value will be used for court, tax filings or resolving disputes among heirs. Spending it when no one needs a formal report is one of the mistakes families make.
estate.pathTitle: Do I Need an Appraisal Before Selling Inherited Property?

estate.q: Dad died over a year ago and we never got an appraisal. Is it too late?
alts: retrospective appraisal date of death
appraisal for a past date
late date of death valuation
can you appraise a house as of when mom died
estate.a: No. A certified appraiser can value a house as of a past date, usually the date of death, even when the report is written months later. This is called a retrospective appraisal, and it documents the value for the inventory, the estate's accountant and the heirs' tax basis. A value set close to the date of death is easier to support, so do not wait longer than needed.
estate.pathTitle: Washington Probate & Estate Glossary

estate.q: What's the difference between an appraisal and a CMA for an estate house?
alts: appraisal vs comparative market analysis
CMA or appraisal for probate
Is a realtor's market analysis the same as an appraisal?
estate.a: An appraisal is an independent, certified opinion of value by a licensed appraiser following USPAP, with an inspection and written report that can be used for legal, tax, lending and court purposes. A CMA is a broker's pricing opinion based on recent sales, used to set a listing price, and does not carry the same legal weight. Use an appraisal when the number will be reported for taxes, relied on by a court or used to divide the estate.
estate.pathTitle: Appraisal vs. CMA: What's the Difference for Estate Property?

estate.q: Can we just use Zillow to price mom's house?
alts: Zestimate inherited house accurate
online home value estimate estate property
Redfin estimate for probate pricing
why not use an online estimate
estate.a: No. Online tools assume a house is in average condition, and estate homes rarely are. They cannot account for deferred maintenance, needed repairs or estate-specific circumstances, and the site says they routinely miss by 10 to 20 percent or more on inherited properties. That leads to overpricing and long market time, or underpricing that leaves the estate's money on the table.
estate.pathTitle: How Do You Price a House in a Trust or Estate?

estate.q: Two agents gave us very different prices for dad's house. Which one is right?
alts: conflicting price opinions inherited house
agents disagree on listing price estate
how to check a realtor's valuation
which home value estimate to trust
estate.a: Ask both agents to show the comparable sales they used and the specific dollar adjustments they made for condition, age and features. A defensible price has math behind it; a guess just has a number. Be wary of choosing whoever gives the highest estimate rather than the most accurate one, especially when you owe the estate fiduciary duties.
estate.pathTitle: Why Valuation Matters for Probate and Inherited Property

estate.q: How do I protect myself if an heir later says I sold the house too cheap?
alts: executor sold below market value claim
documenting the sale price for heirs
fiduciary defensibility estate sale
how executor justifies the sale price
estate.a: Build a documented file as the sale happens. Keep a valuation-based pricing analysis or appraisal, condition photos, comparable-sales adjustments, records of the marketing, every offer received and the reasons for the accepted price. If a beneficiary later questions the price, the answer is in the file. Skipping the date-of-death appraisal and relying on an online estimate is a common source of executor liability.
estate.pathTitle: Frequently Asked Questions About Probate Real Estate

estate.q: Which repairs are worth doing before selling an estate house?
alts: repairs before selling probate home
what to fix before selling inherited house
best return repairs estate sale
paint and clean before selling mom's house
estate.a: Low-cost, high-impact work usually pays off: deep cleaning and odor removal, neutral interior paint, basic yard cleanup, carpet cleaning or replacement, and minor fixes like faucets and fixtures. Safety issues should always be addressed. The test for anything else is whether it will return more than it costs at closing, unless it would stop a buyer from getting a loan.
estate.pathTitle: What Repairs Should Be Made Before Selling a Probate Home?

estate.q: Should we remodel the kitchen before selling dad's house?
alts: renovate inherited house before selling
kitchen remodel estate property worth it
major renovations before probate sale
full remodel before selling mom's house
estate.a: Usually not. A full kitchen renovation is the single most common over-investment in estate properties; buyers often expect to make their own updates, and a clean, functional kitchen is enough in most cases. The site's example: a $40,000 kitchen renovation might add only $20,000. Full renovations rarely pay for themselves on an estate property.
estate.pathTitle: What Repairs Should Be Made Before Selling a Probate Home?

estate.q: Who pays for repairs on a house that's in probate?
alts: estate funds for repairs
Do heirs pay to fix up the inherited house?
no money in the estate for repairs
paying contractors from the estate
estate.a: Repair costs come from estate funds, and the executor must be able to justify any money spent by the return at closing. If the estate has no cash for repairs, some families use bridge financing or negotiate with contractors for payment at closing, or sell as-is. Some improvements funded from estate accounts require careful documentation and sometimes court approval.
estate.pathTitle: What Repairs Should Be Made Before Selling a Probate Home?

estate.q: If we sell mom's house as-is, do we still have to disclose problems?
alts: seller disclosure Form 17 estate sale
Does the executor fill out a disclosure form?
as-is sale known defects Washington
personal representative disclosure exemption
estate.a: A personal representative selling the estate's house does not have to give the buyer Washington's seller disclosure statement (Form 17), because transfers by a personal representative are exempt. But the estate still may not conceal material defects it knows about. Ask the estate's attorney what to tell buyers about problems you are aware of.
estate.pathTitle: What Repairs Should Be Made Before Selling a Probate Home?

estate.q: Will buyers pay less if we sell the inherited house as-is?
alts: as-is sale price discount
sell inherited house without repairs
as-is vs fix up net proceeds
who buys as-is estate homes
estate.a: Generally, yes. Buyers discount for uncertainty, factoring in repair costs plus a risk premium. But that discount is sometimes smaller than the cost of doing the repairs yourself, especially for older homes with a lot of deferred maintenance. Compare expected net proceeds both ways, including the carrying costs of the extra time repairs take. As-is buyers are often investors and contractors.
estate.pathTitle: Should You Sell an Inherited House As-Is or Fix It Up?

estate.q: Do I owe capital gains on mom's house she bought decades ago for much less?
alts: stepped up basis inherited house
capital gains on inherited home Washington
tax on selling a parent's house
basis of inherited property
estate.a: Generally not on the gain from her lifetime. Inherited property usually gets a stepped-up basis equal to its fair market value at the date of death, so if you sell soon after, there is often little or no taxable gain. If the house rises in value after the death, federal capital gains tax can apply to that later increase. A date-of-death appraisal documents the basis; a CPA can confirm your situation.
estate.pathTitle: What Taxes Do You Pay When Selling an Inherited House in Washington?

estate.q: Does Washington's capital gains tax apply when we sell the inherited house?
alts: Washington capital gains tax real estate
state capital gains inherited home Washington
WA capital gains tax house sale
is there state tax on selling dad's house
estate.a: No. Washington's capital gains tax on long-term gains does not apply to sales of real estate, so selling an inherited Washington house does not trigger it. Other assets in the estate may be different, so ask the estate's tax professional. Federal capital gains tax can still apply to any gain above the stepped-up basis.
estate.pathTitle: What Taxes Do You Pay When Selling an Inherited House in Washington?

estate.q: Do we pay real estate excise tax when the house passes to us, or when we sell it?
alts: REET inherited house Washington
excise tax on inheritance Washington
does the estate pay excise tax at sale
real estate excise tax heir
estate.a: Only when it is sold. Passing a house to heirs by inheritance is exempt from Washington's real estate excise tax, but when the estate or the heirs later sell to a buyer, the sale is taxed like any other, usually paid by the seller at closing. A sale from the estate to an heir is also taxed, which is one reason heirs sometimes take the house as part of their share instead.
estate.pathTitle: What Taxes Do You Pay When Selling an Inherited House in Washington?

estate.q: Does my mom get a new tax basis on the whole house after dad died?
alts: surviving spouse stepped up basis community property
basis on both halves of community property
widow selling house capital gains
spouse inherits house tax basis Washington
estate.a: Often, yes. For federal income tax, inherited property generally takes a new basis equal to its date-of-death value, and for community property both halves usually get the new basis at the first spouse's death, not just the half that belonged to the spouse who died. A date-of-death appraisal documents that value; confirm with a CPA how the home was held.
estate.pathTitle: What Taxes Do You Pay When Selling an Inherited House in Washington?

estate.q: Is there an inheritance tax in Washington that I have to pay?
alts: Washington inheritance tax heirs
do heirs pay tax on what they inherit Washington
estate tax vs inheritance tax
who pays Washington estate tax
estate.a: No. Washington has no separate inheritance tax. It does have a state estate tax, which is paid by the estate before distribution, not by individual heirs, and it applies only above an exclusion amount that depends on the date of death. The federal estate tax applies only to very large estates. The estate's accountant can confirm the figures for the date of death.
estate.pathTitle: What Taxes Do You Pay When Selling an Inherited House in Washington?

estate.q: Do I have to pay my dad's debts out of my own money?
alts: are children responsible for parents' debts Washington
heirs liable for deceased debts
who pays debts after death
insolvent estate heirs
Who is responsible for paying the deceased person's debts?
who pays a dead person's bills
What happens to credit card debt after death?
do I have to pay my mom's credit cards after she died
estate.a: Generally, no. Debts are paid from the estate, not by the heirs personally, though someone who receives a nonprobate asset can be required to contribute. If debts exceed assets, creditors are paid in the order the law sets before anyone inherits. The personal representative publishes a notice to creditors and must pay valid debts before distributing anything.
estate.pathTitle: Washington Probate Deadlines & Key Rules

estate.q: Can the state claim my mom's house for Medicaid if it passed by transfer on death deed?
alts: Medicaid estate recovery nonprobate assets Washington
DSHS claim against inherited house
estate recovery transfer on death deed
Does avoiding probate stop Medicaid recovery?
estate.a: It can. If the person received Medicaid long-term care at 55 or older, or state-funded long-term care at any age, the state can seek repayment from the estate and from nonprobate assets, such as a house passing by transfer on death deed. The personal representative's notice to creditors is also mailed to DSHS. The claim can take much of a parent's house proceeds, so ask the estate's attorney about it early.
estate.pathTitle: Washington Probate Deadlines & Key Rules

estate.q: The estate has no money to make mom's mortgage payments. What can we do?
alts: can't afford mortgage on inherited house
estate account frozen mortgage payments
forbearance after borrower death
mortgage payments while probate is open
estate.a: Call the servicer early, before a payment is missed if possible, and ask what options it offers while the estate is settled, such as a short forbearance or a repayment plan. If heirs cover payments to protect the equity, put it in writing as an advance or loan to the estate and keep proof. The fastest relief is usually a sale, which pays off the loan at closing.
estate.pathTitle: What Happens to the Mortgage When Someone Dies in Washington

estate.q: How do I find out if the property taxes on my mom's house are paid?
alts: check property tax status deceased parent
county treasurer lookup estate house
are dad's property taxes current
unpaid property taxes inherited house
estate.a: Look up the house on the county treasurer's website by address or parcel number and check whether both halves of this year's tax are paid. Find out whether taxes are paid through a mortgage escrow account or directly by the owner. Ask the treasurer to send statements to you as personal representative, and before listing, ask the title company for a preliminary report showing any unpaid taxes.
estate.pathTitle: Property Taxes After a Death in Washington: What Executors and Heirs Need to Know

estate.q: My dad had a property tax deferral. What happens to it now?
alts: senior property tax deferral after death Washington
deferred property taxes due at death
state lien deferred taxes inherited house
can heirs continue a tax deferral
estate.a: With a deferral, the state paid the owner's taxes and holds a lien on the house for the deferred amount, with 5 percent yearly interest. The whole deferred balance comes due when the owner dies, the house is sold or the owner moves out for good. A surviving spouse, domestic partner, heir or devisee who qualifies for the program can choose to keep it going; otherwise it is usually paid from the sale.
estate.pathTitle: Property Taxes After a Death in Washington: What Executors and Heirs Need to Know

estate.q: What is an estate sale and how does it work?
alts: how do estate sales work
estate sale company process
estate liquidation steps
selling everything in mom's house
estate.a: An estate sale is an organized, on-site sale of a home's contents, usually run over one to three days by a professional liquidator who catalogs, prices and stages items. It typically moves through a walk-through consultation, sorting and pricing, advertising, running the sale with tag-down discounts on later days, and cleanup with an itemized settlement statement for the family.
estate.pathTitle: Estate Liquidation & Estate Sales Explained

estate.q: How much do estate sale companies charge?
alts: estate liquidator commission
estate sale company fee percentage
cost of an estate sale
estate sale buyout offer
estate.a: Most work on commission, taking a percentage of total sales rather than charging up front. The site puts commissions typically at 30 to 50 percent, depending on scope, the value of the contents, location and extra services such as full cleanout. Smaller estates may carry a higher percentage or a minimum fee, and some liquidators offer a flat-rate buyout of all the contents. Get a written contract.
estate.pathTitle: Estate Liquidation & Estate Sales Explained

estate.q: When should family take keepsakes, before or after the estate sale?
alts: family items before estate sale
clear out house options inherited
what to do with dad's belongings before selling
donate or dispose estate contents
estate.a: Before. Heirs should take items of personal or sentimental value before any estate sale or liquidation. After that, remaining items can go to an estate sale, items with no sale value can be donated, and the rest removed and disposed of. Coordinate with all heirs first, and document contents before a major cleanout so valuables and important papers are not lost.
estate.pathTitle: Preparing the Property for Sale

estate.q: What is probate, and why does my parent's estate have to go through it?
alts: What is probate and why is it required?
what does probate mean
Why do we have to go to court after my mom died?
probate explained washington
what is the point of probate
estate.a: Probate is the court process for settling a person's estate after they die: validating the will, appointing the executor (personal representative), notifying creditors, paying debts and distributing what is left to the heirs. In Washington it is filed in superior court, and most estates are then handled with little court involvement. It is needed mainly when the person owned real estate in their name alone, or significant assets with no beneficiary designation or co-owner.
estate.pathTitle: Understanding Probate & Legal Authority

estate.q: Does every estate have to go through probate?
alts: Do all estates have to go through probate?
How do I know if probate is required in my state?
how do I know if my dad's estate needs probate
is probate always required when someone dies
probate required or not washington
estate.a: No. Probate is needed for property titled in the person's name alone with no beneficiary named. Property that passes by title or designation skips it: a house in a living trust, joint tenancy with right of survivorship, a transfer on death deed recorded before the death, and accounts or policies with a living beneficiary. If everything in the person's name is worth $100,000 or less after liens, a small estate affidavit may work, but it cannot transfer real estate, so a house in their name alone usually means probate.
estate.pathTitle: Washington Probate Deadlines & Key Rules

estate.q: What's the difference between dying with a will and dying without one?
alts: What is the difference between testate (with a will) and intestate (without a will)?
testate vs intestate
what does intestate mean
What changes if dad left a will versus no will?
estate.a: Testate means the person left a valid will; intestate means they did not. A will says who receives the probate estate and names an executor, who still has to be appointed by the court. Without one, Washington's intestacy law decides who inherits, starting with a surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and then descendants, and the court appoints an administrator in a set order of priority.
estate.pathTitle: Washington Probate & Estate Glossary

estate.q: What is a small estate affidavit?
alts: What is small estate probate/affidavit?
small estate affidavit washington how it works
how small does an estate have to be to avoid probate
collect a bank account without probate small estate
estate.a: It is a sworn statement that lets a successor collect a person's personal property, such as a bank account or car, without probate. In Washington it can be used when the whole probate estate, including any real estate, is worth $100,000 or less after liens, and 40 days have passed since the death. It cannot transfer real estate, so a house in the person's name alone usually still means probate.
estate.pathTitle: Washington Probate & Estate Glossary

estate.q: What happens to the mortgage on mom's house while it's in probate?
alts: What happens to a house with a mortgage during probate?
mortgage during probate washington
Who pays dad's mortgage while the estate is open?
does the mortgage get paid off when the owner dies
estate.a: The mortgage does not go away. It stays a lien on the house, interest keeps running, and the personal representative normally keeps the payments current from estate funds, along with the property taxes and insurance. If payments stop, the loan falls behind and can eventually go to foreclosure, costing the family the equity. Tell the servicer about the death and ask to be confirmed as a successor in interest. When the house sells, the loan is paid off from the proceeds at closing.
estate.pathTitle: What Happens to the Mortgage When Someone Dies in Washington

estate.q: How does a living trust avoid probate?
alts: How do trusts avoid probate?
how does a living trust work after someone dies
Why doesn't a trust have to go through probate?
living trust probate how it works
estate.a: Property the trust actually owns passes under the trust's terms, not through probate. The person who created the trust controls it while alive; after their death a successor trustee named in it takes over and can manage or sell the trust's house, usually showing authority with a certification of trust. The key is that the house was deeded into the trust. A house left in the person's own name usually goes through probate first, even when a will sends everything to the trust.
estate.pathTitle: The House Is in a Living Trust

estate.q: What happens to dad's bank account that was only in his name?
alts: What happens to bank accounts held solely in the deceased’s name?
bank account in deceased person's name only
Can I get money out of mom's checking account after she died?
who can access a dead parent's bank account
estate.a: A bank account in the person's name alone, with no beneficiary designation, usually goes through probate. If the whole probate estate, including any real estate, is worth $100,000 or less after liens, a successor can collect it with a small estate affidavit 40 days after the death. Otherwise it waits for the personal representative, who can act only after the superior court appoints them and issues letters. In the meantime, note what accounts exist, but do not close them yet.
estate.pathTitle: Understanding Probate & Legal Authority

estate.q: How are mom's jewelry and personal belongings divided after she dies?
alts: How are personal items and jewelry handled?
who gets mom's jewelry after she dies
dividing personal belongings in an estate
What happens to dad's furniture and keepsakes in probate?
estate.a: A will can give specific instructions about personal items, and the executor it names carries them out. Nothing should be handed out until the estate has been properly administered, because distributing too early can make the executor personally liable. When it is time, heirs take items of personal or sentimental value first, before any estate sale or liquidation; the rest can go to an estate sale, be donated, or be removed and disposed of.
estate.pathTitle: Preparing the Property for Sale

estate.q: What is an executor?
alts: What is an executor (or personal administrator)?
executor meaning
What's the difference between an executor and a personal representative?
what does it mean to be named executor in a will
estate.a: An executor is the person a will names to settle the estate. Washington's term is personal representative, which also covers an administrator the court appoints when there is no will. Being named does not give authority by itself; the executor becomes the personal representative only when the court appoints them. The job is collecting assets, paying debts, filing taxes and distributing what remains to the heirs, as a fiduciary acting in the estate's and beneficiaries' interest.
estate.pathTitle: Washington Probate & Estate Glossary

estate.q: Do I have to be the executor just because I'm named in the will?
alts: Am I required to serve as an executor if I am named in the will?
can I refuse to be executor
Can I say no to being my dad's executor?
decline executor role washington
estate.a: No. Being named in the will does not by itself make you the executor; the person named must petition the court to be appointed. If the named personal representative is unable or unwilling to serve, the court appoints an administrator to fill the same role. An executor who has already started can resign and have a successor appointed, or bring in a professional fiduciary to handle some or all of the administration.
estate.pathTitle: Who Has Authority to Sell Probate Property?

estate.q: The person named as executor won't start probate. What can we do?
alts: What if the executor refuses to start probate?
executor won't open probate
named executor not filing probate washington
nobody has opened probate for dad's estate
estate.a: You are not stuck waiting. The named executor has no authority until the court appoints them, and if the person named is unable or unwilling to serve, the court appoints an administrator instead. Anyone holding the original will must deliver it to the court or the named executor within 30 days of learning of the death. Where there is no will and the family members with priority do not petition within 40 days, the court may appoint someone else. A probate attorney can explain how to get the estate opened.
estate.pathTitle: You Inherited a House, or a Share of One

estate.q: Is the executor's fee taxable income?
alts: do I pay tax on an executor fee
Should I take an executor fee or just my inheritance?
personal representative fee income tax
estate.a: Yes. A fee paid to the executor is taxable income to the executor, while an inheritance generally is not. An executor who is also an heir can choose to take no fee, so when the executor would receive the money either way, waiving the fee can leave more in the family. A CPA can confirm whether that holds for your estate.
estate.pathTitle: Understanding Your Legal Duties as Executor

estate.q: Do I have to pay income tax on a house I inherited?
alts: Do beneficiaries pay income tax on inherited property?
is inherited property taxable income
income tax on an inheritance from my parents
Is my inheritance counted as income?
estate.a: Generally not just for inheriting it. An inheritance generally is not taxable income, and Washington has no separate inheritance tax. Tax comes in when the house is sold: federal capital gains tax applies only to gain above the stepped-up basis, the value at the date of death, so there is often little or no gain on a sale soon after the death. Washington's capital gains tax does not apply to real estate. A CPA can confirm your situation.
estate.pathTitle: What Taxes Do You Pay When Selling an Inherited House in Washington?

estate.q: What tax returns does the executor have to file for the estate?
alts: What taxes must be filed during probate (final income tax, estate tax)?
final tax return for a deceased parent
Does the estate have to file a tax return?
estate tax return washington executor
estate.a: Usually the deceased's final personal income tax return and any required estate income tax returns, and, depending on the estate's size, an estate tax return. Washington has its own estate tax with a relatively low exemption, separate from the federal one, and many estates owe no federal tax but still owe, or must file, the Washington estate tax. An executor who fails to file required returns can be pursued by the IRS, so bring in a CPA early.
estate.pathTitle: Working With Professionals

estate.q: What happens if dad's estate owes more than it's worth?
alts: What is an insolvent estate (more debts than assets)?
estate has more debt than assets
What if there isn't enough money in the estate to pay the bills?
my parent died owing more than they had
estate.a: That is an insolvent estate: its debts are larger than its assets. Heirs are not personally liable for the decedent's debts, though someone who receives a nonprobate asset can be required to contribute toward them. Creditors are paid in the order the law sets before anyone inherits. Nonintervention powers are available only to a solvent estate; without them, selling the house generally needs a court order and the court's confirmation, unless the will authorizes the sale.
estate.pathTitle: Washington Probate & Estate Glossary

estate.q: How long will it take to settle my parent's estate?
alts: How long does the probate process take?
probate timeline washington
how many months does probate take
When will mom's estate be finished?
What makes probate take so long?
What causes delays in probate?
Why is my dad's probate dragging on?
probate delays washington
What can hold up settling mom's estate?
estate.a: There is no fixed length, but the creditor period sets a floor. Creditors have four months from the first publication of the notice to creditors, so most Washington estates stay open at least four months, and most take six months to a year when there is a house to sell, a tax return to file or a disagreement to resolve. The house itself can often be sold well before the estate closes.
estate.pathTitle: Washington Probate Deadlines & Key Rules

estate.q: What happens when we first go to court to open probate?
alts: What happens at the first court appearance?
first probate hearing what to expect
How does the court appoint an executor?
opening probate in court washington
estate.a: In Washington the petition is filed in superior court with the original will, usually through a probate attorney. The court may admit the will and appoint the executor as soon as the petition is presented, heirs are notified after the appointment, and letters issue once the oath is filed and any bond is posted. Without a will, the surviving spouse gets 10 days' notice of someone else's petition unless they waive it. Most estates are then handled with little court involvement.
estate.pathTitle: Washington Probate Deadlines & Key Rules

estate.q: Can we sell mom's house while probate is still open?
alts: Can the house be sold while probate is still open?
Do we have to wait until probate is finished to sell the house?
can you list a house during probate washington
Is the executor allowed to sell dad's house before the estate is closed?
estate.a: Usually, yes. Once the court appoints the executor and issues letters testamentary, the executor can list, market, negotiate and close a sale while other parts of the estate are still being settled. Most Washington estates have nonintervention powers, so no court approval is needed for the sale. A court-supervised estate may need a hearing and confirmation. The sale does not have to wait for the creditor period to end.
estate.pathTitle: Can You Sell a House During Probate in Washington State?

estate.q: Can we start cleaning out mom's house right after she dies, or can one of us live there?
alts: Can the family clean out or live in the deceased's house right away?
When can we start clearing out dad's house after he passed?
Can my brother move into mom's house while the estate is being settled?
clean out parents house after death how soon
estate.a: Plan the cleanout now, but do not rush it. Coordinate with the heirs about personal and family items first; the actual cleanout can start once everyone agrees what to keep, donate and discard, and nobody should take items before a proper inventory. While the estate is in probate, the personal representative controls the house, not a family member living there. If someone stays, put rent, or payment of taxes, insurance and utilities, in a written agreement.
estate.pathTitle: What Should an Executor Do First With a House?

estate.q: When do the heirs actually get their inheritance?
alts: How and when do beneficiaries actually receive their inheritance?
How long until I get my share of mom's estate?
when do beneficiaries get paid from an estate
Will I get the house itself or money from the estate?
estate.a: At the end, after creditors and expenses are paid. Distribution is the final handing over of estate property to the heirs or beneficiaries, as cash, as the property itself, or as a share of sale proceeds. The executor must pay the estate's legitimate debts before distributing anything, and creditors have four months after the notice to creditors is first published, so distribution rarely comes quickly.
estate.pathTitle: Washington Probate & Estate Glossary

estate.q: What happens if someone in the family contests mom's will?
alts: What happens if a family member contests the will?
My brother is challenging dad's will. Now what?
will contest washington what happens
Does a will contest hold up the estate?
estate.a: It becomes a court matter. A will contest challenges the will's validity, for example over capacity, undue influence or how it was signed, and must be filed within four months after the will is admitted to probate or rejected, with the personal representative served within 90 days. Court proceedings may follow, and a contested will can delay appointment by months. An experienced probate attorney is essential, and a mediator can sometimes resolve disputes without litigation.
estate.pathTitle: When You Need Extra Help

estate.q: How do siblings settle disagreements during probate?
alts: How are disputes between siblings handled in probate?
My siblings and I can't agree on anything about mom's estate. What are our options?
sibling dispute probate washington
What is TEDRA?
What happens if heirs or beneficiaries do not get along?
my brothers and sisters are fighting over mom's estate
estate.a: Most disagreements are about value or timing, and an independent appraisal everyone relies on settles many of them. Heirs can also buy one another out. Washington's Trust and Estate Dispute Resolution Act (TEDRA) lets everyone sign a binding agreement without a hearing, or ask the court to decide. A mediator can sometimes resolve disputes without litigation. While the estate is in probate, the personal representative decides about the house; it is not a vote.
estate.pathTitle: Washington Probate Deadlines & Key Rules

estate.q: What can we do if the executor is misusing the estate's money?
alts: What if the executor is accused of stealing or mismanaging funds?
I think my sister is taking money from mom's estate as executor
executor stealing from estate washington
Can the court remove an executor who mismanages the estate?
estate.a: An executor owes a duty of loyalty and cannot use estate assets for personal benefit; one who favors an heir unfairly can be sued by the other beneficiaries. If the personal representative has breached a duty, abused their authority or wrongfully neglected the estate, an heir can petition the court, which can restrict their powers, remove them and appoint someone else, or order other relief. Start by asking in writing for the inventory, and keep copies.
estate.pathTitle: You Inherited a House, or a Share of One

estate.q: How do we handle dad's car after he died?
alts: What happens to a car or vehicle title after death?
Can I get mom's car without going through probate?
transfer car after death washington small estate
estate.a: A car is personal property. If everything in the person's name, real estate included, is worth $100,000 or less after liens, a successor can collect personal property such as a car with a small estate affidavit 40 days after the death, without probate. The affidavit cannot transfer real estate, so a house in the person's name alone usually means probate, and assets owned solely in the person's name then generally go through it.
estate.pathTitle: Washington Probate & Estate Glossary

estate.q: Mom lived in Washington but owned a house in another state. What happens to that house?
alts: How do you transfer out-of-state property (ancillary probate)?
What is ancillary probate?
Does dad's vacation home in another state need its own probate?
ancillary probate out of state house
estate.a: It may need a second, local probate in that state, called ancillary probate. That means working with attorneys licensed in that state in addition to the Washington attorney. The property also needs local help with appraisal, maintenance and the eventual sale. The same applies in reverse: a Washington house owned by someone who lived elsewhere usually needs an ancillary probate here.
estate.pathTitle: When You Need Extra Help

estate.q: How is probate closed in Washington?
alts: How do you formally close a probate case?
What is a declaration of completion?
How does the executor finish and close mom's estate?
close estate washington probate
estate.a: In most Washington estates, which are administered with nonintervention powers, the personal representative closes the estate by filing a declaration of completion. Heirs then have 30 days to ask the court to review it or the fees. If no one does, the fees are deemed reasonable, the estate is deemed properly settled, and the personal representative is discharged. An estate stays open at least until the four-month creditor claim period has run.
estate.pathTitle: Washington Probate & Estate Glossary

estate.q: How does mom's house get put in my name after probate?
alts: How do you transfer a deed into a beneficiary's name?
How do I get the deed to dad's house changed to me?
transfer house to heir washington deed
What deed does the executor sign to give me the house?
estate.a: If the house went through probate, the personal representative signs a personal representative's deed conveying it to the heir, the same kind of deed used for a buyer. The title company will want certified letters and, usually, proof of nonintervention powers. A deed takes effect against later buyers once it is recorded with the county. Passing a house to heirs by inheritance is exempt from the real estate excise tax.
estate.pathTitle: Washington Probate & Estate Glossary

estate.q: What do I do about mom's mail and utilities after she died?
alts: What happens to the deceased person's mail and utilities?
Should I cancel dad's utilities now that he's gone?
forward mail after death
Who pays the utility bills on the house after a death?
estate.a: Forward the mail and keep the utilities on. Have the post office forward mail to an address where you can watch for bills, financial statements and other important correspondence. Keep heat, electricity and water on to prevent frozen pipes, mold and other damage; canceling them to save money is a common mistake. Utilities, mortgage payments and insurance on estate property should keep being paid from estate funds.
estate.pathTitle: Your First 30 Days as Executor

professional.q: Which kind of lawyer do I need after my mom died and left a house?
alts: What type of attorney handles an estate with real estate in it?
my dad passed away which lawyer do I call first
Who helps settle an estate when there's a house involved?
attorney for deceased parent's house washington
professional.a: Usually a probate attorney. A probate attorney handles estate administration after a death, including the court process, creditor issues, and the transfer or sale of property. If the estate includes real property, a probate attorney is typically one of the first professionals involved. Estate planning, elder law, family law and real estate attorneys cover other situations.
professional.pathTitle: Probate and Estate Attorneys in Washington State

professional.q: Do I have to hire a lawyer for probate in Washington?
alts: Is an attorney required for probate in WA?
can I do probate myself without a lawyer
probate without attorney washington
Does the executor or personal representative need a probate lawyer?

does the executor have to hire a probate attorney
Do I legally need a lawyer for probate?
do I really need a lawyer for probate
is a probate attorney required in washington
professional.a: No. Washington State does not require an attorney for probate. But the process involves court filings, legal deadlines and documentation that can be hard to handle alone, especially when real estate is involved. A probate attorney guides the executor or personal representative through filing with the court, notifying creditors, inventorying assets and transferring property to the heirs. The guide notes most families find an experienced attorney saves time, money and family conflict.

professional.q: How soon after my parent dies should I contact a probate attorney?
alts: When is the right time to call a probate lawyer?
how long can I wait to hire a probate attorney
Should I talk to an attorney right away after a death in the family?
probate attorney when to call
professional.a: As soon as possible after a loved one passes. There are legal deadlines for filing with the court and for notifying creditors, and early guidance helps avoid costly mistakes. A probate attorney handles the required court filings, creditor notices and asset inventory documentation, and works alongside real estate professionals when a home has to be sold.

professional.q: What's the difference between an estate planning attorney and a probate attorney?
alts: estate planning lawyer vs probate lawyer
Which attorney writes wills and trusts?
Do I need an estate planner or a probate attorney for my parents?
Who do I see to plan ahead versus after someone dies?
What is the difference between a probate attorney and an estate planning attorney?
probate attorney vs estate planning attorney
professional.a: It comes down to timing. An estate planning attorney helps people plan ahead, creating wills, trusts, powers of attorney and directives for how assets should be handled. A probate attorney handles estate administration after a death, including the court process, creditor issues, and the transfer or sale of property. In short, estate planning happens before a death; probate deals with the estate afterward.
professional.pathTitle: Real Estate Guidance for Probate & Estate Attorneys

professional.q: What does an elder law attorney do, and when does my family need one?
alts: Do I need an elder law attorney for my mom?
elder law attorney medicaid guardianship
Who handles Medicaid planning and long-term care legal issues?
lawyer for an aging parent moving to assisted living
professional.a: An elder law attorney focuses on the legal needs that come with aging: long-term care planning, Medicaid eligibility, guardianship, conservatorship and incapacity planning. Their work can also include powers of attorney, advance directives, veterans' benefits and the legal side of moving to assisted living or memory care. They help families decide about care, housing and assets before a crisis. When the family home is involved, an elder law attorney is often the most important advisor.

professional.q: Do I need a real estate attorney to sell my parents' house?
alts: Is a lawyer required to sell a house in Washington?
real estate attorney needed for home sale
When should I hire a real estate lawyer for an inherited house?
Does every home sale need an attorney?
professional.a: Not always. Many transactions do not require one. A real estate attorney may be helpful when a sale involves contracts, disputes, title problems, ownership questions, easements, litigation or other legal complexity, for example when ownership is unclear, several people disagree about what should happen with the property, or a title issue creates delays. When legal complexity arises, an attorney can be an important part of the team.

professional.q: Who fixes a title or ownership problem on an inherited house?
alts: There's a problem with the deed on my dad's house, who do I call?
inherited house title issue lawyer
Can a real estate attorney help when heirs disagree about who owns the house?
who handles boundary or easement disputes
professional.a: Often a real estate attorney. Real estate attorneys often help with title problems, ownership disputes, deed questions, easements, boundary issues and other legal matters tied to property rights. When the house is being sold, title professionals also research the ownership history, identify liens or encumbrances and resolve title defects. For estate properties, the title search is especially important to confirm that the personal representative or trustee has proper authority to sell.

professional.q: We're divorcing and own a house together. What kind of attorney handles that?
alts: divorce attorney house division
Who deals with the family home in a divorce?
family law attorney vs divorce attorney for property
lawyer to split our house in a divorce
professional.a: A divorce or family law attorney. A divorce attorney handles asset division, spousal support, parenting plans and court filings, and works to make sure the family home or other real property is fairly addressed in the overall settlement. A family law attorney handles custody, parenting plans, guardianship and spousal support, and that work often intersects with real estate when a home or shared assets must be part of a legal resolution.

professional.q: Can we sell the house while our divorce is still going on?

house buyout divorce value
professional.a: In many cases, yes, though it depends on court orders, agreements between the parties and the legal structure of the proceeding. If one person wants to buy out the other, that requires an agreed-upon and defensible market value. A shared, objective market value is often the most important tool for moving a family law property matter forward.

professional.q: What's the difference between an appraisal and a real estate agent's price opinion?

Why get an appraisal for my mom's estate house?
professional.a: A certified appraiser gives an objective, defensible opinion of value backed by formal methodology and local market data. Unlike a broker's price opinion, a certified appraisal is built on structured analysis and documented evidence. Appraisal reports are accepted by courts, lenders and the IRS, and are often required in probate, estate settlement, divorce, tax appeals and senior housing decisions. That difference can help prevent a dispute or protect a fiduciary.

CMA vs appraisal for probate
Can I use a realtor's CMA for a date-of-death value?
Does an agent's market analysis count as an appraisal?
professional.a: No. A comparative market analysis (CMA) is produced by most listing agents and reflects a general price range based on nearby sales. It is not a formal appraisal, and it typically does not account for the home's condition in a documented, methodology-based way. Some situations, such as date-of-death valuations, call for a formal appraisal.

professional.q: Why would we need a CPA when selling Mom's house?
alts: Do I need an accountant when my parent sells their home?
CPA for an inherited property sale
What does a CPA do in probate?
tax help selling parents house washington
professional.a: Because selling or transferring real estate can have tax consequences. When a senior is leaving a longtime home or a property is going through probate, a CPA can help identify tax implications, coordinate financial records, and support decisions that affect timing, proceeds and potential liabilities. CPAs and financial advisors also advise on estate tax obligations, capital gains, stepped-up basis and whether holding or selling makes more financial sense.
professional.pathTitle: Real Estate Guidance for CPAs and the Families They Advise

professional.q: Should I see a CPA or a financial planner about my parent's estate?
alts: CPA vs financial planner difference
financial advisor or accountant for an inheritance
Who handles taxes and who handles investments after a death?
Do I need both a CPA and a financial planner?
professional.a: Often both. A CPA focuses mainly on taxes: filing returns, calculating tax owed and advising on tax strategy. A financial planner takes a broader view, covering investments, retirement income, long-term care planning and overall financial goals. For estate matters, many families benefit from working with both.

professional.q: Do I need a financial advisor if I inherit my parents' house?
alts: inherited a house should I talk to a financial advisor
What is stepped-up basis on an inherited home?
capital gains on an inherited house who can help
Who explains the taxes on inherited property?
professional.a: Not always required, but often very helpful. Inheriting real estate has tax implications, especially capital gains and the stepped-up basis. When you inherit a home, its tax basis is stepped up to the market value at the time of the original owner's death, not what they paid. That often greatly reduces or eliminates capital gains tax if you sell soon after inheriting. A financial advisor or CPA can explain how it applies before you decide.

professional.q: What's the difference between a bookkeeper and a CPA?
alts: bookkeeper vs accountant
Do I need a bookkeeper or a CPA for my dad's business?
bookkeeper or CPA difference
professional.a: A bookkeeper maintains the day-to-day financial records: recording transactions, reconciling accounts, tracking receivables and payables, and keeping the books current. A CPA is a licensed accountant who can prepare and sign tax returns, perform audits and give formal accounting opinions. The two roles complement each other rather than substitute for each other; clean books from a bookkeeper make a CPA's work faster, cheaper and more accurate at tax time.

professional.q: My dad owned a small business and a rental. As executor, why do his books matter?
alts: executor inherited business records
estate with rental property bookkeeping
Do I need a bookkeeper to settle an estate with a business?
my mom's business books are a mess after she died
professional.a: Because most estate steps depend on them. When the person who died owned a business or rental property, the executor inherits responsibility for its financial records. The business has to be valued, a final return filed, outstanding obligations identified and assets distributed accurately. Messy books make all of that harder. Getting records in order early is often the difference between a straightforward settlement and a prolonged one, and that work comes before the CPA's.

professional.q: How do I choose a bookkeeper, and what should I ask?

how to pick a bookkeeper
hiring a bookkeeper when the books are way behind
what to look for in a bookkeeper for a family business
professional.a: Look for someone whose experience matches the size and complexity of the business, who is comfortable with the software you already use, and who explains your financial position in plain language rather than only producing reports. Ask how often you will hear from them, what a typical month looks like, and how they handle a backlog if the books have fallen behind.

professional.q: What is an aging life care manager?

care manager for an elderly parent
Who coordinates my mom's care and her doctors?
aging life care manager washington
professional.a: An aging life care manager, also called a geriatric care manager, is a trained professional, often a social worker or registered nurse, who helps older adults and families with the challenges of aging. They assess physical, emotional and environmental needs, coordinate medical care, and act as an advocate during major transitions. Services often include in-home assessments, care plans, coordination with doctors and facility placement guidance.

professional.q: How is a care manager different from a home caregiver?

Do I need a caregiver or a care manager for my dad?

difference between in-home caregiver and geriatric care manager
professional.a: They do different jobs. A home caregiver gives hands-on daily help, such as bathing, meals or mobility. A care manager works at a higher level: assessing needs, creating care plans, communicating with doctors and facilities, and guiding family decisions. Many families benefit from having both working together.

professional.q: When should we hire a care manager for Mom, and does Medicare pay for it?
alts: signs we need a geriatric care manager
I live out of state and my dad needs someone local

care manager cost who pays
professional.a: Common times are when a parent's health or memory is declining and the family isn't sure what help is needed, when family lives far away and needs a local advocate, after a hospitalization changes care needs, or when deciding between in-home care and a facility. Medicare generally does not pay. Most care management is private pay, though some long-term care insurance policies may cover the fees.

who pays a senior living advisor

assisted living placement service cost

It is still good to ask how an advisor is paid before you start working together. An advisor assesses care needs, preferences and budget, and compares options such as assisted living, memory care and adult family homes.

alts: senior living advisor vs geriatric care manager
Do I need a placement advisor or a care manager?
who helps find assisted living vs who coordinates care
professional.a: A senior housing advisor focuses mainly on finding the right place to live, whether assisted living, memory care, independent living or an adult family home. A care manager takes a broader role, coordinating medical care, family communication and long-term care planning. Many families benefit from both. Advisors can be involved earlier than most families think; even if a move is 6 to 12 months away, an early conversation helps families understand options and costs.

professional.q: What does a senior move manager do?
alts: senior move manager services
help moving my mom into assisted living
Who helps a parent downsize and pack up a longtime home?
senior move management washington
professional.a: A senior move manager helps older adults and families plan and manage the physical and emotional process of leaving a longtime home, whether the move is to assisted living, a family member's home or a smaller residence. Services typically include space planning, sorting belongings, coordinating donation and disposal, packing, overseeing the move, and unpacking and resettling. Many also coordinate with estate sale companies and cleanout crews to handle what remains.

professional.q: Do I need a senior move manager or just a moving company?

Is a regular mover enough for my dad's downsizing?
difference between moving company and move manager
who sorts and unpacks for seniors when they move
professional.a: It depends on how much help is needed. Moving and relocation services handle packing, transport, storage and delivery. A senior move manager covers the larger process, including space planning, sorting and organizing belongings, donation and disposal, and unpacking and resettling in the new home. They work at the client's pace, with attention to the emotional weight of leaving a home full of memories.

professional.q: How do estate sale companies get paid?

how much does an estate sale company charge

estate liquidator fees

professional.q: Should we hold the estate sale before or after listing Mom's house?

estate sale timing and the house sale
estate sale before listing the home

estate sale during probate washington

choosing an estate sale company questions

professional.q: What's the difference between Medicare and Medicaid?

what is dual eligibility

professional.a: Choose one yourself; Real Property Planning does not refer clients to attorneys. Look for experience with Washington probate specifically and familiarity with the county where the estate is being administered. Confirm any lawyer's license with the Washington State Bar Association (wsba.org). Reach out early, ideally within the first two weeks, since Washington probate has filing deadlines.
